mount.description: The name a page: join on a display's socket finds this cell under. [a-z0-9-], 1..=64 characters, and none of the names the API already answers.

chromium_path.description: The Chromium-based browser binary from this machine's package system. Required, with no default and no search path: meclaw ships no browser and never goes looking for one.

user_data_dir.description: The profile directory the browser runs in. Empty means the cell names one of its own under /tmp, creates it, and removes it when the cell ends.

extra_args.description: Extra browser flags. The flags the cell owns (--headless, --remote-debugging-*, --user-data-dir, --disk-cache-dir) are refused, and so is --no-sandbox: the browser's sandbox belongs to the package it came from.

max_pages.description: How many pages may be open at once. Above it the oldest SUSPENDED page is closed to make room, and if none is suspended the request is refused with too_many_pages -- never a silent displacement.

suspend_after_ms.description: How long a page nobody is watching stays open. Then its target is closed and its context kept; 0 never suspends.

throttle_after_ms.description: How long a page may produce frames without a pause before the cell slows its acknowledgements to two a second and reports state throttled.

screencast.description: How the picture is cut and how fast it is acknowledged. format jpeg or png, quality 1..=100, max_width and max_height in device pixels, max_fps the pace of the acknowledgement rather than a promise about the page.

sandbox.description: The CELL's ceiling, as a cgroup v2 cap and nothing else (config.md, The cap alone). Required: a browser cell with no declared ceiling does not start, and a restricted profile must carry limits, since one without a cap is trusted under another name. It is not the browser's sandbox: that belongs to the package, and this cell neither switches it on nor off.

external_timeout_ms.description: The A-timeout around every CDP round trip and around the spawn. This cell is long-running, so there is no message-timeout behind it.

startup_timeout_ms.description: How long the browser has to answer Browser.getVersion before the spawn is given up.

description.purpose: One browser for one member: a browser context per identity, a page per card, and each page's picture on a topic of a display's socket. The topology hears about pages -- one opened, one moved, one went quiet, one came back -- and never about a frame.
description.use_when: Wherever an application wants to put a web page on a screen instead of a summary of one. Instantiate it once per member, give it the mount a display's page: joins should reach, and point chromium_path at the browser this machine has installed. Wire four edges in the same mutation: open, close and navigate in, and the page lane back out.
description.not_in_scope: No browser of its own: the binary is a prerequisite out of the distribution's package system, and this template ships none. No sandbox switch, no --no-sandbox and no flag of any kind about the browser's own confinement. No persistence of a logged-in session -- a context is ephemeral by design, so closing it is what logging out means and a restart is a logged-out browser. No video codec: the picture is a JPEG screencast, and a second stage is a later wave.
description.emits_meaning: page: the state of one page, on every change -- opening, active, background, suspended, reopened, throttled, closed -- carrying its full address with fragment, its title, its context, its viewport, its content_type and, after somebody used it, active_at as epoch milliseconds in text. error: a spawn, a CDP or a crash failure with its error_code. receipt: the answer to one of the four verbs, with ok or the refusal's code.
description.consumes_meaning: One tool_call turn whose text is the JSON args of one verb: in_open {page, url, context?, viewport?}, in_navigate {page, url}, in_close {page}, in_context_close {context}. There is no verb for an input -- a pointer, a key or a run of text travels on the link the picture comes down, never as a message.
examples: PORTS - Entry: a tool_call turn naming one of the four verbs. Exit: a receipt per message and a page emission per state change, both on hop.route.

{"name": "in_open", "arguments": {"page": "card-7", "url": "https://example.com/", "viewport": {"width": 960, "height": 600, "dpr": 2, "mobile": false}}} -> receipt ok, then page {state: opening} and page {state: active} once somebody joins page:card-7
a ninth page while eight are open and none is suspended -> receipt error_code too_many_pages, and not one of the eight is displaced
a browser whose own sandbox does not hold -> error error_code spawn_failed, and no page at all
